§ 03 · The tools, briefly

An editor that disappears.

Source Serif at 19 pixels. A 64-character measure. No toolbar floating in your face. Markdown if you want it, keyboard shortcuts if you need them, and an autosave that ships every 14 seconds. We don't show word counts unless you ask. We don't suggest titles. We don't run grammar checks. You're not writing tweets.

Drafts are versioned forever. Revert any paragraph to its state on any date. Export the whole archive as a single, valid EPUB whenever you like.

DRAFT · ISSUE 028
SAVED 14s ago
On second drafts, and the people who never see them.

For seven years I refused to publish anything I hadn't rewritten at least four times. Then I started working a job that didn't have time for it.

What I learned, in those years, was that most readers can tell the difference between a third and a fifth draft. They just don't have the vocabulary to say so.

Numbers, when you actually want them.

Open rate, reply rate, churn. That's the dashboard. No engagement scores, no virality multipliers, no notifications when someone leaves. You can dig into a city map of your readers if you want — it's behind two clicks. The default is a single page that takes 14 seconds to scan.

Import from Substack, beehiiv, Ghost, or Mailchimp with one CSV. We re-verify every address on the way in, so you don't ship your first issue into a graveyard.

Your list is yours. We mean it.

Export the full subscriber list at any time — with timestamps, source, and verified status — as a CSV you can carry to any other tool tomorrow. No "data portability tier." No locked features for paying customers. The migration is one button. We've had 38 writers leave for other platforms; we kept their referrals on file as a courtesy.

Custom domains on every plan. We host the DNS. You hold the contract.

§ 06 · From the writers
§ 07 · A few questions

Things sensible people ask before signing up.

§ FAQ.01

How do migrations from Substack actually work — paid subscriptions and all?

+

We pull your subscriber list and your paying customers via the Substack export. Stripe customers transfer with payment methods intact — no one has to re-enter a card. The full migration averages 38 minutes; the longest on record was three hours.

§ FAQ.02

Why no app? My readers ask, and I'd like to be able to point them somewhere.

+

An app introduces a feed; a feed pits writers against one another for attention. We decided that trade-off wasn't worth it. The reading experience on web and email is the same — Source Serif, 64-character measure, no chrome.

§ FAQ.03

What does deliverability look like at 50,000+ subscribers?

+

We send from dedicated IP pools warmed per publication. Median inbox placement across Gmail, Outlook, Fastmail, and iCloud is 98.4% on lists over 50K. SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and BIMI are configured on every custom domain at setup — there's nothing for you to copy-paste.

§ FAQ.04

Can I keep my existing domain and brand without a "powered by" line?

+

Yes. No "powered by" badge on either plan. Your domain, your design tokens (we expose 28 CSS variables), your name on the masthead. We don't put our logo in your reader's inbox.

§ FAQ.05

What happens to my archive and subscribers if Manuscript ever shuts down?

+

A 90-day sunset commitment is written into our terms. You'd receive a full export — subscribers, issues as standards-compliant HTML and EPUB, paid customers as a Stripe portable bundle — plus six months of email forwarding on your custom domain at no cost.
